findings.title: Mutual exclusion check for `age` and `timestamp` fails when either value is `0`
findings.body: In `BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`, the check uses `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):` (truthiness) instead of checking `is not None` (or key presence). Because `0` is a valid value for both `age` (a report delivered immediately) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), a report containing both `"age": 0` and a non-zero `"timestamp"` (or vice versa) will only fail validation on one of the two fields or pass `validate_timestamp` when `age == 0`. In addition, if neither `age` nor `timestamp` is provided, neither field validator runs and the report is accepted without either field. Check `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp") is not None`.

findings.title: Non-dict element in report list causes unhandled `TypeError` (HTTP 500) instead of 422
findings.body: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, `raw_data` is verified to be a `list`, and then each element `report` is passed to `BrowserReportSerializer(data=report)`. If a client sends a list containing a primitive such as `[0]` or `["foo"]`, `serializer.is_valid()` populates `serializer.errors` with `{"non_field_errors": [...]}` but when `validate_timestamp` or `validate_age` (or any code touching `self.initial_data.get(...)`) runs, or if `report` is not a mapping, DRF's serializer validation works only up to `run_validation`, yet if `report` is a dict with `None` or if `self.initial_data` is accessed when not a dict, `AttributeError` can be raised. More importantly, `TestBrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint` has no check for non-object items in the list.

findings.title: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs event IDs with the wrong nodestore payloads when any event is missing
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict mapping only the found `node_id`s to their data (or in an order/subset not guaranteed to match `error_ids` 1-to-1 when some keys are missing). Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` in `fetch_error_details` shifts all subsequent `event_id`s whenever a node is missing from nodestore, associating each `event_id` with a different event's `title`, `timestamp`, and `message`. Look up each node via `events.get(node_id)` while iterating over `zip(error_ids, node_ids)` instead.

findings.title: `request.user.id` raises `AttributeError` when authenticated with an OrgAuthToken or ProjectKey
findings.body: `ProjectPreprodArtifactAssembleEndpoint.post` now records analytics with `user_id=request.user.id` before checking anything else. This endpoint uses `ProjectReleasePermission` and explicitly supports org auth tokens (see lines 137-138: `if is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth):`). When a request is authenticated via an `OrgAuthToken` (or `AnonymousUser`), `request.user` is an `AnonymousUser` whose `.id` is `None` in Django, or in Sentry's custom `AnonymousUser` may not have `.id` or may be `None`. Verify `request.user.id if request.user.is_authenticated else None` is used so token-authenticated CI uploads do not fail.

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, when `searchQuery.trim()` is empty (lines 61-63), `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` directly without filtering out `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`['is_segment', 'project_id', 'received']`). Those hidden attributes are only excluded inside the `filter` callback on lines 65-69 when `searchQuery` is non-empty, which means `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are visible by default and only disappear once the user types into the search box. Filter out `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` before checking `!searchQuery.trim()`.

findings.title: Replacing `FlexBox` with `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` drops `height: 100%` on the waterfall container
findings.body: `FlexBox` previously had `height: 100%; flex-grow: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column;`. Replacing it with `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` omits `height: 100%` (since `Flex` only sets `display: flex`, `flex-direction`, and `flex`). In parent containers that size children via percentage height rather than flex layout, the trace waterfall container will no longer fill the available height.
